title: Large Language Models Help Humans Verify Truthfulness -- Except When They Are Convincingly Wrong
authors_or_organization: Chenglei Si, Navita Goyal, Sherry Tongshuang Wu, Chen Zhao, Shi Feng, Hal Daume III, Jordan Boyd-Graber (Stanford, UMD, CMU, NYU Shanghai, NYU, Microsoft Research)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: One author affiliated with Microsoft Research; funding not checked
limitations: Lay Prolific crowdworkers (16 per condition, 20 claims each, 1500 annotations); adversarial Wikipedia claims (FoolMeTwice); binary true/false judgments; gpt-3.5-turbo; Wikipedia retrieval; single session; no domain expertise or accountability; condition-level n is small.

title: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines
authors_or_organization: Nelson F. Liu, Tianyi Zhang, Percy Liang (Stanford)
data_collection_dates: 2023 (system outputs collected at time of study; exact dates not reported in excerpt read)
limitations: Audit of four 2023 commercial systems (Bing Chat, NeevaAI, perplexity.ai, YouChat) on 1450 queries; annotators judged support, not decision makers using outputs; systems have changed since; correlation between citation precision and perceived utility appears to be computed across system-level averages (few points).

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making
authors_or_organization: Helena Vasconcelos, Matthew Jorke, Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Tobias Gerstenberg, Michael S. Bernstein, Ranjay Krishna
limitations: Maze-solving task with simulated AI and 'perfect' explanations (authors' own limitation); crowdworkers; 5 studies N=731; low ecological validity for professional diligence; earlier pre-registered Wikipedia QA studies with inline answer highlights were stopped early and not reported.

title: In Search of Verifiability: Explanations Rarely Enable Complementary Performance in AI-Advised Decision Making
authors_or_organization: Raymond Fok, Daniel S. Weld (University of Washington; Allen Institute for AI)
publication_date: arXiv v4 2024-02-01 (reported as AI Magazine 2024; venue not verified in this session)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Co-author affiliated with Allen Institute for AI; funding not checked
limitations: Theory/position paper synthesizing prior studies; no new data; classification of tasks as verifiable is the authors' judgment.

title: "I'm Not Sure, But...": Examining the Impact of Large Language Models' Uncertainty Expression on User Reliance and Trust
authors_or_organization: Sunnie S. Y. Kim, Q. Vera Liao, Mihaela Vorvoreanu, Stephanie Ballard, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan (Princeton; Microsoft)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Four of five authors affiliated with Microsoft (an LLM search provider)
limitations: Pre-registered online experiment N=404 US lay participants; medical trivia-style questions; fictional LLM search engine with 50% designed accuracy (authors note low accuracy); single session; link-click vs self-report discrepancy partly due to modeling choices.

title: Citations and Trust in LLM Generated Answers
authors_or_organization: Yifan Ding, Matthew Facciani, Amrit Poudel, Ellen Joyce, Salvador Aguinaga, Balaji Veeramani, Sanmitra Bhattacharya, Tim Weninger (Univ. of Notre Dame; Deloitte AI Center for Excellence)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Funded by DARPA (contracts HR001121C0168, HR00112290106); co-authors from Deloitte & Touche LLP
limitations: Prolific lay participants N=303, self-generated questions, self-reported trust only (no accuracy/error-detection measure); citation checking tracked by mouse interaction; publication venue not verified (arXiv version read).

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
authors_or_organization: Miles Turpin, Julian Michael, Ethan Perez, Samuel R. Bowman (NYU Alignment Research Group; Cohere; Anthropic)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Authors affiliated with Cohere and Anthropic (model developers)
limitations: Model-behavior experiment (no human subjects); GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0 (older models); BIG-Bench Hard and BBQ benchmarks; biasing features are synthetic.

title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
authors_or_organization: Yanda Chen, Joe Benton, Ansh Radhakrishnan, Jonathan Uesato, et al. (Anthropic Alignment Science Team)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Authored by Anthropic (developer of Claude models evaluated); note this worker is an Anthropic model
limitations: Model-behavior study; hint-based faithfulness measure on multiple-choice benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA); synthetic RL environments; not a human-verification study.

title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models
authors_or_organization: Hannah Rashkin, Vitaly Nikolaev, et al. (Google Research)
limitations: Annotation-protocol paper; completion times reflect trained crowd raters with justification requirements in pilot; not a decision-making study; benchmarks (QReCC, WoW, CNN/DM, ToTTo).

title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients: A Randomized Clinical Vignette Survey Study
authors_or_organization: Sarah Jabbour et al. (University of Michigan; full author list not verified in this session)
limitations: Full article page retrieved via WebFetch (an automated summarizer); values below were extracted by that tool from the article text, not read line by line; final ~7.5k characters not processed. Vignettes, not live care; Grad-CAM heatmap explanations only; no time-per-case measure.

title: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears in the results
data_collection_dates: Browsing data March 1-31, 2025; search results re-collected April 7-17, 2025
limitations: Read via WebFetch summarizer (not line-by-line); observational browsing data (900 US adults, KnowledgePanel Digital); lay consumer search; only first three cited links counted; correlational (queries that trigger AI summaries differ from others).

title: Towards Verifiable Text Generation with Symbolic References (SymGen)
authors_or_organization: Lucas Torroba Hennigen, Shannon Zejiang Shen, Aniruddha Nrusimha, Bernhard Gapp, David Sontag, Yoon Kim (MIT; Good Data Initiative)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Supported by Liberty Mutual through MIT Quest for Intelligence
limitations: 60 Prolific annotators, 4 summaries each (within-subject), sports box-score summaries, single planted numeric error within 2 units; no significance tests located; tabular data only; provenance correct by construction.

title: HoT: Highlighted Chain of Thought for Referencing Supporting Facts from Inputs
authors_or_organization: Tin Nguyen, Logan Bolton, Mohammad Reza Taesiri, Trung Bui, Anh Totti Nguyen, et al. (Auburn University; University of Alberta)
publication_date: 2026-06 (Transactions on Machine Learning Research; arXiv v6 2026-06-27)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: NSF grants; donations from NaphCare Foundation and Adobe Research; API credits from together.ai
limitations: 63 students, 10 items each, balanced 50/50 correct/incorrect LLM answers, 2-minute cap per item; arithmetic and reading-comprehension tasks; SDs large; significance tests not located in section read.

title: Comparing Traditional and LLM-based Search for Consumer Choice: A Randomized Experiment
authors_or_organization: Sofia Eleni Spatharioti, David M. Rothschild, Daniel G. Goldstein, Jake M. Hofman (Microsoft Research NYC)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: All authors Microsoft Research (provider of Bing search/chat)
limitations: MTurk participants (Exp1 N=90; Exp2 N=120); consumer vehicle comparison tasks; one designed error item; Exp1 GPT-3.5 vs Exp2 GPT-3 (not comparable across experiments); the LLM tool gave no source links, traditional search gave links.

title: How well do LLMs cite relevant medical references? An evaluation framework and analyses (SourceCheckup)
authors_or_organization: Kevin Wu, Eric Wu, Ally Casasola, Angela Zhang, Kevin Wei, Teresa Nguyen, Sith Riantawan, Patricia Shi, Daniel Ho, James Zou (Stanford et al.)
publication_date: arXiv v1 2024-02-03 (a later peer-reviewed version reportedly exists; not verified)
limitations: Automated GPT-4 judge validated on N=284 statement-source pairs against three physicians; model versions now outdated; measures support of citations, not user verification behavior.

title: AI-Powered Lawyering: AI Reasoning Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and the Future of Legal Practice
authors_or_organization: Daniel Schwarcz, Sam Manning, Patrick Barry, David R. Cleveland, JJ Prescott, Beverly Rich
publication_date: 2025 (manuscript; journal publication reported but not verified)
data_collection_dates: not located (late 2024 implied by use of o1-preview)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Funded by Fredrikson & Byron PA, Robins Kaplan LLC, Univ. of Minnesota and Univ. of Michigan law schools; OpenAI and vLex made platforms freely available (no financial support per authors)
limitations: 127 upper-level law students (not practicing lawyers); hallucinations counted only as fabricated sources (miscitations excluded, fn 138); hallucination counts very small; verification behavior not directly observed.

title: Show Me the Work: Fact-Checkers' Requirements for Explainable Automated Fact-Checking
authors_or_organization: Greta Warren, Irina Shklovski, Isabelle Augenstein (University of Copenhagen; Linkoping University)
limitations: Qualitative semi-structured interviews with 10 professional fact-checkers; stated requirements, not observed verification performance.
